## Overview

LRP77a is the **baseline-ability sensitivity fit** for [LRP77](../lrp-rli-dose-077/). It is the identical dose-response model with the **baseline-skill cluster** added to the adjustment set: letter-sound knowledge ($L$), expressive vocabulary ($E$) and phoneme blending ($B$). These are the reflective indicators of latent general ability $g$ in the revised DAG, alongside the already-adjusted baseline reading $W_{\text{pre}}$.

**Each adjuster is that child's verified t1 value, broadcast across all three transitions.** This matters more than it sounds. Until #587 the fit used each transition's *own* starting wave — t1 skills in period 1, but t2 skills in period 2 and t3 skills in period 3. Those later values are themselves downstream of earlier intervention and attendance, so the model was conditioning on a treatment-affected time-varying covariate rather than on a baseline: it could block part of the very path it was measuring, and it was not the pre-randomisation ability adjustment it was published as. The repair changes 98 of the 156 fitted rows' ability values. `ability_baseline_wave="transition_start"` retains the old behaviour as an explicitly labelled comparator; it must not be read as a baseline sensitivity.

**Why.** The revised DAG carries $GA \to IS$ (latent), so if abler children attended more (Frank 2012) then $g$ is a common cause of attendance and outcome and the measured adjustment set does not identify an attendance effect — and because attendance is **not** randomised, randomisation does not rescue it. Conditioning on the baseline-skill cluster probes that path with observed proxies.

**Compare with LRP77.** Report how the attendance association changes after adding the baseline-skill proxies, with uncertainty. Stability does not show that latent ability is unrelated to attendance; a smaller slope does not measure the amount of confounding removed. The comparison also depends on measurement error, collinearity and any change in fitted rows. These proxies do not establish control for $g$.

See the LRP77 report for the estimand, the presence and attendance terms, and the $G = 2 - \text{group}$ coding (G=1 = immediate intervention). Every attendance coefficient remains an adjusted association.
